_comment: A player Infantry unit stands in Shield Wall between two enemy Infantry units spawned directly ahead and directly behind it. Team 0 stays put by default; both team-1 units march straight at the only enemy they can see, so the wall ends up struck from front and rear at once -- genuine encirclement, not just a flank brush. Watch soldier_summary.broken_count in the state dump: verified locally (seed 12345) it reads 0 while only the rear unit is in contact (~tick 210-240), jumps sharply once the front unit also closes and both sides are FIGHTING (~tick 270, over a third of the defenders broken at once), then falls back to 0 once the rear attacker is destroyed and only one side remains -- the individually surrounded soldiers rejoin their formation the instant the encirclement clears, exactly as the mechanic intends. A handful of soldiers occasionally show broken again later even with only one attacking unit left -- real flank/envelopment contact from a single unit's own soldiers wrapping around a defender, not a second attacker.
